events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $3.74 (model confidence 0.90)
events.body:
This is a RydeTAXI metered trip, so distance actually driven flows straight into the fare, and the refund formula for an unexempted detour is Σ(extra_km of non-exempt segments) × per-km rate, rate = distance_fare ÷ distance_km = $35.17 ÷ 24.9 km = $1.4124.../km [F1][F7][RD-2].

Two off-route segments exist: 22:57–23:03 adding 1.14 km [F3] and 23:21–23:24 adding 1.51 km [F4]; RD-1 makes each a deviation until RD-3, RD-4 or RD-5 excuses it [F3][F4][RD-1]. No exemption applies. The driver only says he followed his GPS after rerouting [F10] — RD-4 requires a traffic incident on the replaced optimal stretch reported before the detour, and there are none [F13][RD-4]; the speed-band records on East Coast Parkway and Airport Boulevard are band 3 (20–29 km/h) [F11][F12], which is not band 1 or 2 and in any case cannot exempt a segment on its own [RD-4]. There is no rider-requested stop, and no driver route-change proposal accepted by the rider before leaving the optimal route [F8][F9][RD-3][RD-5]. Both segments are therefore non-exempt detours.

Amount: 1.14 km + 1.51 km = 2.65 km of unexempted extra distance; 2.65 km × $1.4124/km = $3.7429, rounded to $3.74 [F3][F4][F7][RD-2]. The broader billed excess of $4.41 for the full +3.1 km [F5] is not refunded beyond this, because RD-2 refunds only the unexempted segment km, and the waiting line is $0.00 here so no RD-3(c) issue arises.

No account flag: the driver's profile shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0, so the RD-6 precondition for a repeated-breach account referral is not met [F16][RD-6].

RIDER: We reviewed your fare dispute. You were taken off the most direct route twice: once adding 1.14 km and once adding 1.51 km, and neither was for an approved reason. Since this was a metered trip, that extra distance was billed to you.

We are refunding $3.74 into your Ryde account as a voucher. This covers only the extra distance on those two segments, so it is less than the full excess shown on your bill. No further action is needed from you.

DRIVER: We reviewed a rider dispute about your route on this trip. Two stretches where you left the most direct route added 1.14 km and 1.51 km, and no exemption applied — following your GPS after rerouting does not excuse a detour, since no traffic incident on the replaced stretch was reported beforehand.

Outcome: $3.74 of the fare is being refunded to the rider as a Ryde voucher. This breach is recorded on your account; no account flag is being applied. Keep to the most direct route unless a valid exemption applies.
